item.title: Re: A Physically - Impossible Restraining Order
item.content:encoded:
1) Don't provide hints; be obvious. Be as straightforward as possible.

2) "Central narrative" isn't how it will be presented, it's the story of the item in question. How you will be formatting is under the "Page Layout" section; we need to know the history of the item, and you haven't really provided anything. Sure, we know it's supposed to work, but we know nothing of the item itself. That's a major issue here.

3) All you've done under "Hook" is tell us more about formatting, and not why we should care about the item. In music, the hook is that initial riff that grabs someone and doesn't let go; There's none of that here. You've given a brief description of what it does and then nothing but formatting. We need a reason to care about this thing. Give us on!

item.title: Re: The Spire - needs greenlights
item.content:encoded:
In terms of how it works, it looks pretty solid. The two basic problems are the hook and the why.

The Why: It would be interesting why the reality warper created this tool. Sure, there's the possibility of it happened randomly, but that's no fun; there has to be a reason for why it exists, be it a tool, a weapon, or even a puzzle. In short, there has to be a reason why it exists. In that regard, it would be interesting to see what the others looked like and see if there was some sort of pattern to them.

The Hook: Testing would have been discontinued once the majority of rules were figured out so as to avoid it teleporting. What you need is a reason for people to care about it, what it says about the SPC-U as a whole, or just what kind of niche it fills. In short, why testing was discontinued just isn't interesting when the reason is somewhat obvious, and if it isn't obvious then it needs to be stated.

There just needs to be a reason for people to care about the item.

item.title: Re: additional idea information
item.content:encoded:
If you're having trouble with presenting your concept concisely, you can look at this thread for tips: http://www.scpwiki.com/forum/t-13369776/how-do-i-remain-brief-when-writing-an-scp-concept

Is it okay if I reply to my Idea post with extra information about the concept?

No. Per the Site Rules, you should avoid replying to your own comments, as that generates spam. Furthermore, reviewers should only have to read at maximum 400 words to understand the basics of your core concept. If you attempt to require reviewers to read more than that when they'd already be doing you the favor of assisting with your writing, you may find that fewer people will be willing to review for you in the first place.

item.title: Re: Around the world
item.content:encoded:
Hello Noname1810! lets take a look :)

SAND

+ show block
– hide block

Quick note:
I noticed some grammar errors throughout the post, I would recommend double checking the spelling, as bad grammar can make it harder to understand and accurately critique concepts.

The concept:

• SCP-xxxx is a working compass, observation outside the area of 200m radius from SCP-xxxx on the area within will result as if there is currently no SCP-xxxx and sapient being (having intelligence at least equal to lizards) inside the area. Observers from inside will perceive white fog at the border of the area which can't be seen through.

It could just be me, but this confuses me a bit; "sapient being (having intelligence at least equal to lizards) inside the area". Lizards would be much closer to sentient than sapient, as they aren't self aware and don't share the same complexity as humans (to my knowledge, the same goes for all animals). -are certain animals affected by this too, or is it only humans? if certain animals are affected, how does it relate back to the concept and narrative?

• SCP-xxxx-1 is any sapient being that currently observing SCP-xxxx, other SCP-xxxx-1 or on SCP-xxxx-2
• If there are about 11 to 35 SCP-xxxx-1 at the moment, SCP-xxxx might transfer all SCP-xxxx-1 along with everything thing in their sight and touch to the magnetic South Pole a planet designated as SCP-xxxx-2 in an unknown dimension. When in this area, if SCP-xxxx is destroyed or has a distance more than 10m away from all SCP-xxxx-1 and out of sight, SCP-xxxx will reappears within 10m of the closest SCP-xxxx-1.

• SCP-xxxx-2 has a diameter about 1100km, its surface is made up of places in and out side our dimension, those places are constantly changing when out of observation. Interaction on SCP-xxxx-2 affect those places where they come from (a record of expedition in SCP-xxxx-2 was found in an abandoned house). The only way known to get out of SCP-xxxx-2 is to put SCP-xxxx directly on the magnetic North Pole of the planet.

Currently, the concept feels directionless as there isn't much behind the initial effects and specific details. There also isn't any sort of explanation or purpose for the skips existence shown here, which makes it hard to get invested in the idea.

Along with this, the concept feels overcomplicated, as the skips effects only seem to manifest under fairly specific conditions. There are also other smaller ideas that are only semi-related to the main concept, that don't really add much. ie. the intelligence level of living beings, the north and south poles, the extra dimensional areas.

- Overall, I would recommend simplifying the concept down, try to get an idea of the core concept and trim off anything that doesn't contribute to the main idea.

Some questions I got:
why is SCP-xxxx-2 made up of so many different places?
why do those places change?
why/how can you only get out SCP-xxxx-2 when the compass is put on the North pole?
how do the different dimensions play a part in this?
what is the white fog that occurs around the compass?
why does the compass transport people to an extra dimensional space in certain circumstances?

The narrative:

The foundation found SCP-xxxx after many report of missing in a small town, MTF team was sent in for investigation.
• Expedition 1 summary:
Upon recovering SCP-xxxx, it manifested and transferred 11 researchers and the MTF team to SCP-xxxx-2. After more than 2 years, they became the first people to exit SCP-xxxx-2.
After that SCP-xxxx activated several times and caused lost of many personnel but SCP-xxxx didn’t activate while they tried to test it
• Expedition 2 summary:
Several guards, personnel and D-class was transferred by SCP-xxxx-2, they got out with loss of most people. This expedition gave the foundation a lot of valuable information.

The setup is a little vague, as it doesn't show how the skip itself was found, or what happens immediately after.- Considering the skips anomaly isn't immediately obvious. -Where's the lead-up to the investigations and expeditions? why does the Foundation decide to look further into this?

The middle act, payoff and main conflict don't seem to be shown in the story, which makes the stories events feel flat, and closer to a few instances that don't have much correlation with each other. How should I feel about the story? why should I care about the characters? - Currently the entire narrative seems to be in the expedition logs, which alone won't be able to carry the article.

As for the expeditions themselves, there isn't much here showing actually happens, or much showing how and what the Foundation finds out about the skip. Considering the exploration will play a major role in the narrative, I would recommend showing what the MTFs actually experience, and show how said experiences play a part in the rest of the story.

- as a quick second note, it feels out of character for the Foundation to continue expeditions when personnel are imminent danger, the Foundation would need a strong reason to continue expeditions when they know personnel are likely to be killed.

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no greenlight.

If you would like me review this (or any concept) further, then please feel free to send me a PM or ask via IRC. Response times generally range from 2-12 hours over PMs. If your looking for additional critiques in general, then I would highly recommend contacting the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,

-RED

item.title: Re: Emergency broadcast system from space. Looking for greenlights
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Jungle14. Let’s take a look at your concept.

Yes, an emergency alien broadcast would be intriguing, but the entirely article cannot be based on a series of alien journal entries, can it?

The article has potential, but it’s missing details, a backstory, and potential cliffhanger conclusion. First, please tell us what the actual contents of the broadcast are. You don’t have to elaborate, but we need to know what the actual threat is. Second, I don’t understand why the scientists who made the initial discovery were amnesticised, especially if they already belonged to the Foundation? Third, okay, so after you go into detail of the four broadcasts… so what? What’s the imminent danger? What is the Foundation going to do besides waiting around?

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll take another look. All the best for now!

item.title: Re: Admin Panel
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Osana Akasuki. Let’s take a look at your concept.

So I think you have a solid foundation. The premise is interesting, as is the potential for nifty exploration and testing logs. What I’m mainly concerned about at this point is how the article will look like, because my impression of it from reading the concept is that you’d just be listing a long page of experiments after tweaking certain settings to show various effects taking place in reality.

And then, what? You see, that’s not a coherent narrative. You have an intriguing beginning (discovery) and middle section (testing and escalation of effects), but you’re lacking an ending. It’s not enough to just say this is “God’s Program”, as I have a feeling the Foundation themselves won’t be satisfied with this answer. Was there an actual Maker of the program? If so, what were its intentions?

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll take another look. All the best for now!

item.title: Re: Concept : Ever Burning Flames.
item.content:encoded:
1) If the flames continue to grow then why would they stop at the edge of the city? Especially considering that there are actually more burnables there than in the center of the city? Also, how was it contained? There just seem a lot of things that are ill-defined here, and they should be better defined.

2) Speaking of: The zone of infinite place needs to be better defined. It just feels like it was added to justify the survival of the survivor and the book. If it's going to be part of the SCP, then it needs to be reasonably well-defined.

3) The bottom lines is that you've thrown so much stuff into the SCP without really defining anything that there's just nothing for a reader to grab on to, from the gauntlet to the infinite space, and the overall feel is that you're just throwing stuff at a wall hoping something will stick. Slow down, think it through, and focus on what needs to happen. Just focus on what it needs and see what happens.

item.title: Re: Festive Jello Strikes Back
item.content:encoded:
Got a PM about this, took a look. I'm largely in agreement with Grigori here; what you've got is a pretty bland monster that might have been alright on the mainsite a decade ago, but the concept as it is won't do well on the mainsite today given we have thousands of similarly dangerous entities written, many of them with more narrative to them than just "it wreaks havoc and presumably a GoI made it".

I'm also unsure about the cognitohazard/pheromone explanation, since if the jello itself is constantly secreting the pheromones, how does that trigger its own response only when "prey" is nearby? The backstory of the investigation also makes the Foundation look rather incompetent—if one field agent already went missing, why didn't the later ones take better precautions when investigating? Having a live body cam feed, radioing in their status every few minutes or so, even just sending a drone into the location to scout. It seems kind of silly that the agents' disappearance would be entirely unexplained and necessitate an MTF be sent in to do the same job.

The description of the anomaly being jello containing human remains just makes me think of the Gelatinous Cube from Dungeons & Dragons: https://roll20.net/compendium/dnd5e/Gelatinous%20Cube it also seems a little odd that it would specifically need to be festive jello; I personally don't know anyone who actually eats jello specifically for the holidays. I feel like if you really want to make this specific monster workable, you'd need to make it more distinct from the popular D&D monsters and also have an in-universe reason for why it exists the way it does. Otherwise you have something that's relatively forgettable and will be more likely compared to more interesting monsters in popular culture, rather than being interesting on its own merit.

The audience is constantly kept engaged by a linear narrative starting off with mystery that later unfolds into a deeper investigation of the SCP's origins.

This is a big, big assumption to make here, especially since you haven't finalized what the motives of the GoI are, and it's still unclear what the point of the anomaly actually is. I myself don't really think a draft of the material currently presented would be engaging, since the core anomaly is fairly boring, the effects seem rather randomly applied and not thematically related, and the backstory is rather vague. You'd need to address all of these issues before I would think it reasonable to expect the audience to be "constantly engaged".
